cartridge.name: owasp-asvs-5.0-architecture.md

rules.title: Document session inactivity timeout and absolute maximum lifetime
rules.when: Designing or implementing session management mechanisms for the application
rules.then: Verify that the user's session inactivity timeout and absolute maximum session lifetime are documented, are appropriate in combination with other controls, and that the documentation includes justification for any deviations from NIST SP 800-63B re-authentication requirements.

source.quote: Verify that the user's session inactivity timeout and absolute maximum session lifetime are documented, are appropriate in combination with other controls, and that the documentation includes justification for any deviations from NIST SP 800-63B re-authentication requirements.

rules.title: Document concurrent session limits
rules.when: Defining session policies and concurrent user access limits for accounts
rules.then: Verify that the documentation defines how many concurrent (parallel) sessions are allowed for one account as well as the intended behaviors and actions to be taken when the maximum number of active sessions is reached.

source.quote: Verify that the documentation defines how many concurrent (parallel) sessions are allowed for one account as well as the intended behaviors and actions to be taken when the maximum number of active sessions is reached.

rules.title: Document federated identity and SSO session systems
rules.when: Integrating federated identity management or SSO ecosystems with application sessions
rules.then: Verify that all systems that create and manage user sessions as part of a federated identity management ecosystem (such as SSO systems) are documented along with controls to coordinate session lifetimes, termination, and any other conditions that require re-authentication.

source.quote: Verify that all systems that create and manage user sessions as part of a federated identity management ecosystem (such as SSO systems) are documented along with controls to coordinate session lifetimes, termination, and any other conditions that require re-authentication.

rules.title: Perform session token verification using a trusted backend service
rules.when: Validating user session tokens within the application architecture
rules.then: Verify that the application performs all session token verification using a trusted, backend service.

source.quote: Verify that the application performs all session token verification using a trusted, backend service.

rules.title: Use dynamically generated self-contained or reference tokens
rules.when: Selecting or implementing session management token types
rules.then: Verify that the application uses either self-contained or reference tokens that are dynamically generated for session management, i.e. not using static API secrets and keys.

source.quote: Verify that the application uses either self-contained or reference tokens that are dynamically generated for session management, i.e. not using static API secrets and keys.

rules.title: Ensure reference tokens possess at least 128 bits of entropy
rules.when: Using reference tokens to represent user sessions
rules.then: Verify that if reference tokens are used to represent user sessions, they are unique and generated using a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator (CSPRNG) and possess at least 128 bits of entropy.

source.quote: Verify that if reference tokens are used to represent user sessions, they are unique and generated using a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator (CSPRNG) and possess at least 128 bits of entropy.

rules.title: Generate new session token on authentication and re-authentication
rules.when: A user undergoes user authentication or re-authentication
rules.then: Verify that the application generates a new session token on user authentication, including re-authentication, and terminates the current session token.

source.quote: Verify that the application generates a new session token on user authentication, including re-authentication, and terminates the current session token.

rules.title: Enforce inactivity timeout based on risk analysis
rules.when: Maintaining active user sessions over time
rules.then: Verify that there is an inactivity timeout such that re-authentication is enforced according to risk analysis and documented security decisions.

source.quote: Verify that there is an inactivity timeout such that re-authentication is enforced according to risk analysis and documented security decisions.

rules.title: Enforce absolute maximum session lifetime
rules.when: Managing the total lifespan of user sessions
rules.then: Verify that there is an absolute maximum session lifetime such that re-authentication is enforced according to risk analysis and documented security decisions.

source.quote: Verify that there is an absolute maximum session lifetime such that re-authentication is enforced according to risk analysis and documented security decisions.

rules.title: Disallow further use of session upon termination
rules.when: Session termination is triggered via logout or expiration
rules.then: Verify that when session termination is triggered (such as logout or expiration), the application disallows any further use of the session. For reference tokens or stateful sessions, this means invalidating the session data at the application backend. Applications using self-contained tokens will need a solution such as maintaining a list of terminated tokens, disallowing tokens produced before a per-user date and time or rotating a per-user signing key.

source.quote: Verify that when session termination is triggered (such as logout or expiration), the application disallows any further use of the session. For reference tokens or stateful sessions, this means invalidating the session data at the application backend. Applications using self-contained tokens will need a solution such as maintaining a list of terminated tokens, disallowing tokens produced before a per-user date and time or rotating a per-user signing key.

rules.title: Terminate active sessions when user account is disabled or deleted
rules.when: A user account is disabled or deleted (such as an employee leaving the company)
rules.then: Verify that the application terminates all active sessions when a user account is disabled or deleted (such as an employee leaving the company).

source.quote: Verify that the application terminates all active sessions when a user account is disabled or deleted (such as an employee leaving the company).

rules.title: Option to terminate other active sessions after authentication factor change
rules.when: A successful change or removal of any authentication factor occurs (including password change via reset or recovery and MFA settings update)
rules.then: Verify that the application gives the option to terminate all other active sessions after a successful change or removal of any authentication factor (including password change via reset or recovery and, if present, an MFA settings update).

source.quote: Verify that the application gives the option to terminate all other active sessions after a successful change or removal of any authentication factor (including password change via reset or recovery and, if present, an MFA settings update).

rules.title: Provide easy and visible logout access on authenticated pages
rules.when: Rendering pages that require authentication
rules.then: Verify that all pages that require authentication have easy and visible access to logout functionality.

source.quote: Verify that all pages that require authentication have easy and visible access to logout functionality.

rules.title: Administrator capability to terminate active sessions
rules.when: Administrators need to manage user sessions
rules.then: Verify that application administrators are able to terminate active sessions for an individual user or for all users.

source.quote: Verify that application administrators are able to terminate active sessions for an individual user or for all users.

rules.title: Require re-authentication for sensitive account attribute modifications
rules.when: Modifying sensitive account attributes such as email address, phone number, MFA configuration, or account recovery information
rules.then: Verify that the application requires full re-authentication before allowing modifications to sensitive account attributes which may affect authentication such as email address, phone number, MFA configuration, or other information used in account recovery.

source.quote: Verify that the application requires full re-authentication before allowing modifications to sensitive account attributes which may affect authentication such as email address, phone number, MFA configuration, or other information used in account recovery.

rules.title: Allow users to view and terminate active sessions
rules.when: Users access session management controls and re-authenticate with at least one factor
rules.then: Verify that users are able to view and (having authenticated again with at least one factor) terminate any or all currently active sessions.

source.quote: Verify that users are able to view and (having authenticated again with at least one factor) terminate any or all currently active sessions.

rules.title: Require step-up authentication for highly sensitive transactions
rules.when: Performing highly sensitive transactions or operations
rules.then: Verify that the application requires further authentication with at least one factor or secondary verification before performing highly sensitive transactions or operations.

source.quote: Verify that the application requires further authentication with at least one factor or secondary verification before performing highly sensitive transactions or operations.

rules.title: Federated session lifetime and termination coordination
rules.when: Implementing Relying Party (RP) or Identity Provider (IdP) federation behavior
rules.then: Verify that session lifetime and termination between Relying Parties (RPs) and Identity Providers (IdPs) behave as documented, requiring re-authentication as necessary such as when the maximum time between IdP authentication events is reached.

source.quote: Verify that session lifetime and termination between Relying Parties (RPs) and Identity Providers (IdPs) behave as documented, requiring re-authentication as necessary such as when the maximum time between IdP authentication events is reached.

rules.title: Require user consent or explicit action for session creation
rules.when: Creating a new application session
rules.then: Verify that creation of a session requires either the user's consent or an explicit action, preventing the creation of new application sessions without user interaction.

source.quote: Verify that creation of a session requires either the user's consent or an explicit action, preventing the creation of new application sessions without user interaction.

rules.title: Document function-level and data-specific authorization rules
rules.when: Establishing authorization requirements and access control documentation
rules.then: Verify that authorization documentation defines rules for restricting function-level and data-specific access based on consumer permissions and resource attributes.

source.quote: Verify that authorization documentation defines rules for restricting function-level and data-specific access based on consumer permissions and resource attributes.

rules.title: Document field-level access restriction rules
rules.when: Defining field-level read and write access rules based on consumer permissions and resource attributes
rules.then: Verify that authorization documentation defines rules for field-level access restrictions (both read and write) based on consumer permissions and resource attributes. Note that these rules might depend on other attribute values of the relevant data object, such as state or status.

source.quote: Verify that authorization documentation defines rules for field-level access restrictions (both read and write) based on consumer permissions and resource attributes. Note that these rules might depend on other attribute values of the relevant data object, such as state or status.

rules.title: Document environmental and contextual attributes for security decisions
rules.when: Configuring environmental or contextual security factors in the application
rules.then: Verify that the application's documentation defines the environmental and contextual attributes (including but not limited to, time of day, user location, IP address, or device) that are used in the application to make security decisions, including those pertaining to authentication and authorization.

source.quote: Verify that the application's documentation defines the environmental and contextual attributes (including but not limited to, time of day, user location, IP address, or device) that are used in the application to make security decisions, including those pertaining to authentication and authorization.

rules.title: Document usage of environmental and contextual factors in decision-making
rules.when: Documenting authentication and authorization decision-making mechanisms
rules.then: Verify that authentication and authorization documentation defines how environmental and contextual factors are used in decision-making, in addition to function-level, data-specific, and field-level authorization. This should include the attributes evaluated, thresholds for risk, and actions taken (e.g., allow, challenge, deny, step-up authentication).

source.quote: Verify that authentication and authorization documentation defines how environmental and contextual factors are used in decision-making, in addition to function-level, data-specific, and field-level authorization. This should include the attributes evaluated, thresholds for risk, and actions taken (e.g., allow, challenge, deny, step-up authentication).

rules.title: Restrict function-level access to consumers with explicit permissions
rules.when: Ensuring function-level access control in the application
rules.then: Verify that the application ensures that function-level access is restricted to consumers with explicit permissions.

source.quote: Verify that the application ensures that function-level access is restricted to consumers with explicit permissions.

rules.title: Restrict data-specific access to mitigate IDOR and BOLA
rules.when: Restricting access to specific data items to prevent insecure direct object reference and broken object level authorization
rules.then: Verify that the application ensures that data-specific access is restricted to consumers with explicit permissions to specific data items to mitigate insecure direct object reference (IDOR) and broken object level authorization (BOLA).

source.quote: Verify that the application ensures that data-specific access is restricted to consumers with explicit permissions to specific data items to mitigate insecure direct object reference (IDOR) and broken object level authorization (BOLA).

rules.title: Restrict field-level access to mitigate BOPLA
rules.when: Restricting access to specific fields to mitigate broken object property level authorization
rules.then: Verify that the application ensures that field-level access is restricted to consumers with explicit permissions to specific fields to mitigate broken object property level authorization (BOPLA).

source.quote: Verify that the application ensures that field-level access is restricted to consumers with explicit permissions to specific fields to mitigate broken object property level authorization (BOPLA).

rules.title: Implement adaptive security controls based on context
rules.when: Applying adaptive security controls based on environmental and contextual attributes during new and existing sessions
rules.then: Verify that adaptive security controls based on a consumer's environmental and contextual attributes (such as time of day, location, IP address, or device) are implemented for authentication and authorization decisions, as defined in the application's documentation.

source.quote: Verify that adaptive security controls based on a consumer's environmental and contextual attributes (such as time of day, location, IP address, or device) are implemented for authentication and authorization decisions, as defined in the application's documentation. These controls must be applied when the consumer tries to start a new session and also during an existing session.

rules.title: Enforce authorization rules at a trusted service layer
rules.when: Enforcing application authorization rules to prevent manipulation by untrusted consumers
rules.then: Verify that the application enforces authorization rules at a trusted service layer and doesn't rely on controls that an untrusted consumer could manipulate, such as client-side JavaScript.

source.quote: Verify that the application enforces authorization rules at a trusted service layer and doesn't rely on controls that an untrusted consumer could manipulate, such as client-side JavaScript.

rules.title: Apply changes to authorization values immediately
rules.when: Applying changes to values on which authorization decisions are made
rules.then: Verify that changes to values on which authorization decisions are made are applied immediately.
exceptions: Where changes cannot be applied immediately, such as when relying on data in self-contained tokens, there must be mitigating controls to alert when a consumer performs an action when they are no longer authorized to do so and revert the change.

source.quote: Verify that changes to values on which authorization decisions are made are applied immediately. Where changes cannot be applied immediately, (such as when relying on data in self-contained tokens), there must be mitigating controls to alert when a consumer performs an action when they are no longer authorized to do so and revert the change. Note that this alternative would not mitigate information leakage.

rules.title: Base object access on originating subject permissions
rules.when: Accessing objects via intermediaries or services acting on behalf of a consumer
rules.then: Verify that access to an object is based on the originating subject's (e.g. consumer's) permissions, not on the permissions of any intermediary or service acting on their behalf.

source.quote: Verify that access to an object is based on the originating subject's (e.g. consumer's) permissions, not on the permissions of any intermediary or service acting on their behalf. For example, if a consumer calls a web service using a self-contained token for authentication, and the service then requests data from a different service, the second service will use the consumer's token, rather than a machine-to-machine token from the first service, to make permission decisions.

rules.title: Use cross-tenant controls in multi-tenant applications
rules.when: Developing multi-tenant applications to prevent cross-tenant interaction without permissions
rules.then: Verify that multi-tenant applications use cross-tenant controls to ensure consumer operations will never affect tenants with which they do not have permissions to interact.

source.quote: Verify that multi-tenant applications use cross-tenant controls to ensure consumer operations will never affect tenants with which they do not have permissions to interact.

rules.title: Incorporate multiple security layers for administrative interfaces
rules.when: Securing access to administrative interfaces
rules.then: Verify that access to administrative interfaces incorporates multiple layers of security, including continuous consumer identity verification, device security posture assessment, and contextual risk analysis, ensuring that network location or trusted endpoints are not the sole factors for authorization even though they may reduce the likelihood of unauthorized access.

source.quote: Verify that access to administrative interfaces incorporates multiple layers of security, including continuous consumer identity verification, device security posture assessment, and contextual risk analysis, ensuring that network location or trusted endpoints are not the sole factors for authorization even though they may reduce the likelihood of unauthorized access.

rules.title: Enable only latest recommended TLS protocol versions
rules.when: Configuring TLS protocol versions in the application
rules.then: Verify that only the latest recommended versions of the TLS protocol are enabled, such as TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3. The latest version of the TLS protocol must be the preferred option.

source.quote: Verify that only the latest recommended versions of the TLS protocol are enabled, such as TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3. The latest version of the TLS protocol must be the preferred option.

rules.title: Enable only recommended cipher suites with forward secrecy
rules.when: Configuring cipher suites for applications
rules.then: Verify that only recommended cipher suites are enabled, with the strongest cipher suites set as preferred. L3 applications must only support cipher suites which provide forward secrecy.

source.quote: Verify that only recommended cipher suites are enabled, with the strongest cipher suites set as preferred. L3 applications must only support cipher suites which provide forward secrecy.

rules.title: Validate mTLS client certificates before use
rules.when: Using mTLS client certificate identity for authentication or authorization
rules.then: Verify that the application validates that mTLS client certificates are trusted before using the certificate identity for authentication or authorization.

source.quote: Verify that the application validates that mTLS client certificates are trusted before using the certificate identity for authentication or authorization.

rules.title: Enable proper certificate revocation mechanisms
rules.when: Configuring TLS certificate revocation such as OCSP Stapling
rules.then: Verify that proper certification revocation, such as Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) Stapling, is enabled and configured.

source.quote: Verify that proper certification revocation, such as Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) Stapling, is enabled and configured.

rules.title: Enable Encrypted Client Hello in TLS settings
rules.when: Configuring application TLS settings to prevent sensitive metadata exposure during handshake
rules.then: Verify that Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) is enabled in the application's TLS settings to prevent exposure of sensitive metadata, such as the Server Name Indication (SNI), during TLS handshake processes.

source.quote: Verify that Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) is enabled in the application's TLS settings to prevent exposure of sensitive metadata, such as the Server Name Indication (SNI), during TLS handshake processes.

rules.title: Use TLS for all client and external service connectivity
rules.when: Establishing connectivity between a client and external facing HTTP-based services
rules.then: Verify that TLS is used for all connectivity between a client and external facing, HTTP-based services, and does not fall back to insecure or unencrypted communications.

source.section: V12.2 HTTPS Communication with External Facing Services
source.quote: Verify that TLS is used for all connectivity between a client and external facing, HTTP-based services, and does not fall back to insecure or unencrypted communications.

rules.title: Use publicly trusted TLS certificates for external services
rules.when: Deploying certificates for external facing services
rules.then: Verify that external facing services use publicly trusted TLS certificates.

source.section: V12.2 HTTPS Communication with External Facing Services
source.quote: Verify that external facing services use publicly trusted TLS certificates.

rules.title: Use encrypted protocols for all inbound and outbound connections
rules.when: Making inbound and outbound connections to and from the application
rules.then: Verify that an encrypted protocol such as TLS is used for all inbound and outbound connections to and from the application, including monitoring systems, management tools, remote access and SSH, middleware, databases, mainframes, partner systems, or external APIs.

source.section: V12.3 General Service to Service Communication Security
source.quote: Verify that an encrypted protocol such as TLS is used for all inbound and outbound connections to and from the application, including monitoring systems, management tools, remote access and SSH, middleware, databases, mainframes, partner systems, or external APIs. The server must not fall back to insecure or unencrypted protocols.

rules.title: Validate certificates received by TLS clients
rules.when: Establishing communication from a TLS client to a TLS server
rules.then: Verify that TLS clients validate certificates received before communicating with a TLS server.

source.section: V12.3 General Service to Service Communication Security
source.quote: Verify that TLS clients validate certificates received before communicating with a TLS server.

rules.title: Use transport encryption for internal HTTP-based services
rules.when: Connecting between internal HTTP-based services within the application
rules.then: Verify that TLS or another appropriate transport encryption mechanism used for all connectivity between internal, HTTP-based services within the application, and does not fall back to insecure or unencrypted communications.

source.section: V12.3 General Service to Service Communication Security
source.quote: Verify that TLS or another appropriate transport encryption mechanism used for all connectivity between internal, HTTP-based services within the application, and does not fall back to insecure or unencrypted communications.

rules.title: Use trusted certificates for internal TLS connections
rules.when: Using internal TLS connections between internal services
rules.then: Verify that TLS connections between internal services use trusted certificates.
exceptions: Where internally generated or self-signed certificates are used, the consuming service must be configured to only trust specific internal CAs and specific self-signed certificates.

source.section: V12.3 General Service to Service Communication Security
source.quote: Verify that TLS connections between internal services use trusted certificates. Where internally generated or self-signed certificates are used, the consuming service must be configured to only trust specific internal CAs and specific self-signed certificates.

rules.title: Use strong authentication for internal service communications
rules.when: Communicating internally within a system across microservices or endpoints
rules.then: Verify that services communicating internally within a system (intra-service communications) use strong authentication to ensure that each endpoint is verified.

source.section: V12.3 General Service to Service Communication Security
source.quote: Verify that services communicating internally within a system (intra-service communications) use strong authentication to ensure that each endpoint is verified. Strong authentication methods, such as TLS client authentication, must be employed to ensure identity, using public-key infrastructure and mechanisms that are resistant to replay attacks. For microservice architectures, consider using a service mesh to simplify certificate management and enhance security.

rules.title: Identify and classify sensitive data
rules.when: Creating and processing sensitive data within the application
rules.then: Verify that all sensitive data created and processed by the application has been identified and classified into protection levels.

source.quote: Verify that all sensitive data created and processed by the application has been identified and classified into protection levels. This includes data that is only encoded and therefore easily decoded, such as Base64 strings or the plaintext payload inside a JWT. Protection levels need to take into account any data protection and privacy regulations and standards which the application is required to comply with.

rules.title: Document protection requirements for sensitive data
rules.when: Defining protection levels for sensitive data
rules.then: Verify that all sensitive data protection levels have a documented set of protection requirements including encryption, integrity, retention, logging, and access controls.

source.quote: Verify that all sensitive data protection levels have a documented set of protection requirements. This must include (but not be limited to) requirements related to general encryption, integrity verification, retention, how the data is to be logged, access controls around sensitive data in logs, database-level encryption, privacy and privacy-enhancing technologies to be used, and other confidentiality requirements.

rules.title: Transmit sensitive data only in body or headers
rules.when: Sending sensitive data to the server
rules.then: Verify that sensitive data is only sent to the server in the HTTP message body or header fields, and that the URL and query string do not contain sensitive information.

source.quote: Verify that sensitive data is only sent to the server in the HTTP message body or header fields, and that the URL and query string do not contain sensitive information, such as an API key or session token.

rules.title: Prevent sensitive data caching in server components
rules.when: Handling sensitive data across server components
rules.then: Verify that the application prevents sensitive data from being cached in server components, such as load balancers and application caches, or ensures that the data is securely purged after use.

source.quote: Verify that the application prevents sensitive data from being cached in server components, such as load balancers and application caches, or ensures that the data is securely purged after use.

rules.title: Prevent sending sensitive data to untrusted parties
rules.when: Transmitting data to third parties or user trackers
rules.then: Verify that defined sensitive data is not sent to untrusted parties to prevent unwanted collection of data outside of the application's control.

source.quote: Verify that defined sensitive data is not sent to untrusted parties (e.g., user trackers) to prevent unwanted collection of data outside of the application's control.

rules.title: Implement documented protection controls for sensitive data
rules.when: Implementing controls for sensitive data
rules.then: Verify that controls around sensitive data related to encryption, integrity verification, retention, logging, and privacy technologies are implemented as defined in the documentation.

source.quote: Verify that controls around sensitive data related to encryption, integrity verification, retention, how the data is to be logged, access controls around sensitive data in logs, privacy and privacy-enhancing technologies, are implemented as defined in the documentation for the specific data's protection level.

rules.title: Configure caching mechanisms to prevent web cache deception
rules.when: Configuring caching mechanisms and handling non-existent files
rules.then: Verify that caching mechanisms are configured to only cache responses with expected content types and do not contain sensitive dynamic content, and return 404 or 302 for non-existent files.

source.quote: Verify that caching mechanisms are configured to only cache responses which have the expected content type for that resource and do not contain sensitive, dynamic content. The web server should return a 404 or 302 response when a non-existent file is accessed rather than returning a different, valid file. This should prevent Web Cache Deception attacks.

rules.title: Return minimum required sensitive data and mask complete data
rules.when: Returning sensitive data for application functionality
rules.then: Verify that the application only returns the minimum required sensitive data, and mask complete data in the user interface unless specifically viewed.

source.quote: Verify that the application only returns the minimum required sensitive data for the application's functionality. For example, only returning some of the digits of a credit card number and not the full number. If the complete data is required, it should be masked in the user interface unless the user specifically views it.

rules.title: Subject sensitive information to data retention classification
rules.when: Managing sensitive information storage and lifecycle
rules.then: Verify that sensitive information is subject to data retention classification, ensuring outdated or unnecessary data is deleted automatically or on a defined schedule.

source.quote: Verify that sensitive information is subject to data retention classification, ensuring that outdated or unnecessary data is deleted automatically, on a defined schedule, or as the situation requires.

rules.title: Remove sensitive information from user-submitted file metadata
rules.when: Processing user-submitted files
rules.then: Verify that sensitive information is removed from the metadata of user-submitted files unless storage is consented to by the user.
exceptions: unless storage is consented to by the user

source.quote: Verify that sensitive information is removed from the metadata of user-submitted files unless storage is consented to by the user.

rules.title: Clear authenticated data from client storage on session termination
rules.when: Terminating a client session or connection
rules.then: Verify that authenticated data is cleared from client storage after the client or session is terminated.

source.quote: Verify that authenticated data is cleared from client storage, such as the browser DOM, after the client or session is terminated. The 'Clear-Site-Data' HTTP response header field may be able to help with this but the client-side should also be able to clear up if the server connection is not available when the session is terminated.

rules.title: Set sufficient anti-caching HTTP response header fields
rules.when: Configuring HTTP response headers for browsers
rules.then: Verify that the application sets sufficient anti-caching HTTP response header fields so that sensitive data is not cached in browsers.

source.quote: Verify that the application sets sufficient anti-caching HTTP response header fields (i.e., Cache-Control: no-store) so that sensitive data is not cached in browsers.

rules.title: Restrict sensitive data in browser storage
rules.when: Storing data in browser storage mechanisms
rules.then: Verify that data stored in browser storage does not contain sensitive data, with the exception of session tokens.
exceptions: with the exception of session tokens

source.quote: Verify that data stored in browser storage (such as localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, or cookies) does not contain sensitive data, with the exception of session tokens.

rules.title: Maintain an inventory of application logging
rules.when: Documenting logging across the technology stack
rules.then: Verify that an inventory exists documenting the logging performed at each layer of the application's technology stack, events, formats, storage, usage, access control, and retention.

source.quote: Verify that an inventory exists documenting the logging performed at each layer of the application's technology stack, what events are being logged, log formats, where that logging is stored, how it is used, how access to it is controlled, and for how long logs are kept.

rules.title: Include necessary metadata in each log entry
rules.when: Generating log entries
rules.then: Verify that each log entry includes necessary metadata that allows for a detailed investigation of the timeline when an event happens.

source.quote: Verify that each log entry includes necessary metadata (such as when, where, who, what) that would allow for a detailed investigation of the timeline when an event happens.

rules.title: Synchronize time sources and use UTC timestamps in logs
rules.when: Configuring time sources for logging components
rules.then: Verify that time sources for all logging components are synchronized, and that timestamps use UTC or include an explicit time zone offset.

source.quote: Verify that time sources for all logging components are synchronized, and that timestamps in security event metadata use UTC or include an explicit time zone offset. UTC is recommended to ensure consistency across distributed systems and to prevent confusion during daylight saving time transitions.

rules.title: Restrict log storage and broadcast destinations to inventory
rules.when: Storing or broadcasting application logs
rules.then: Verify that the application only stores or broadcasts logs to the files and services that are documented in the log inventory.

source.quote: Verify that the application only stores or broadcasts logs to the files and services that are documented in the log inventory.

rules.title: Ensure logs are readable and correlatable by log processors
rules.when: Processing and correlating logs
rules.then: Verify that logs can be read and correlated by the log processor in use, preferably using a common logging format.

source.quote: Verify that logs can be read and correlated by the log processor that is in use, preferably by using a common logging format.

rules.title: Enforce protection levels when logging sensitive data
rules.when: Logging sensitive data
rules.then: Verify that when logging sensitive data, the application enforces logging based on the data's protection level (e.g., hashing or masking).

source.quote: Verify that when logging sensitive data, the application enforces logging based on the data's protection level. For example, it may not be allowed to log certain data, such as credentials or payment details. Other data, such as session tokens, may only be logged by being hashed or masked, either in full or partially.

rules.title: Log all authentication operations
rules.when: Performing authentication operations
rules.then: Verify that all authentication operations are logged, including successful and unsuccessful attempts, with additional metadata.

source.quote: Verify that all authentication operations are logged, including successful and unsuccessful attempts. Additional metadata, such as the type of authentication or factors used, should also be collected.

rules.title: Log failed authorization attempts and sensitive data access
rules.when: Performing authorization operations or accessing sensitive data
rules.then: Verify that failed authorization attempts are logged, and for L3, log all authorization decisions including sensitive data access without logging the sensitive data itself.

source.quote: Verify that failed authorization attempts are logged. For L3, this must include logging all authorization decisions, including logging when sensitive data is accessed (without logging the sensitive data itself).

rules.title: Log security events and security control bypass attempts
rules.when: Encountering security events or bypass attempts
rules.then: Verify that the application logs the security events defined in documentation and logs attempts to bypass security controls such as input validation, business logic, and anti-automation.

source.quote: Verify that the application logs the security events that are defined in the documentation and also logs attempts to bypass the security controls, such as input validation, business logic, and anti-automation.

rules.title: Log unexpected errors and security control failures
rules.when: Encountering unexpected errors or security control failures
rules.then: Verify that the application logs unexpected errors and security control failures such as backend TLS failures.

source.quote: Verify that the application logs unexpected errors and security control failures such as backend TLS failures.

rules.title: Encode Log Data to Prevent Log Injection
rules.when: Logging component processes data
rules.then: Verify that all logging components appropriately encode data to prevent log injection.

source.quote: Verify that all logging components appropriately encode data to prevent log injection.

rules.title: Protect Logs from Unauthorized Access and Modification
rules.when: Storing logs
rules.then: Verify that logs are protected from unauthorized access and cannot be modified.

source.quote: Verify that logs are protected from unauthorized access and cannot be modified.

rules.title: Securely Transmit Logs to Separate System
rules.when: Transmitting logs for analysis and detection
rules.then: Verify that logs are securely transmitted to a logically separate system for analysis, detection, alerting, and escalation. The aim is to ensure that if the application is breached, the logs are not compromised.

source.quote: Verify that logs are securely transmitted to a logically separate system for analysis, detection, alerting, and escalation. The aim is to ensure that if the application is breached, the logs are not compromised.

rules.title: Return Generic Messages for Errors
rules.when: An unexpected or security-sensitive error occurs
rules.then: Verify that a generic message is returned to the consumer when an unexpected or security-sensitive error occurs, ensuring no exposure of sensitive internal system data such as stack traces, queries, secret keys, and tokens.

source.quote: Verify that a generic message is returned to the consumer when an unexpected or security-sensitive error occurs, ensuring no exposure of sensitive internal system data such as stack traces, queries, secret keys, and tokens.

rules.title: Secure Operation on External Resource Failure
rules.when: External resource access fails
rules.then: Verify that the application continues to operate securely when external resource access fails, for example, by using patterns such as circuit breakers or graceful degradation.

source.quote: Verify that the application continues to operate securely when external resource access fails, for example, by using patterns such as circuit breakers or graceful degradation.

rules.title: Graceful and Secure Failure on Exceptions
rules.when: An exception occurs during processing
rules.then: Verify that the application fails gracefully and securely, including when an exception occurs, preventing fail-open conditions such as processing a transaction despite errors resulting from validation logic.

source.quote: Verify that the application fails gracefully and securely, including when an exception occurs, preventing fail-open conditions such as processing a transaction despite errors resulting from validation logic.

rules.title: Last Resort Error Handler for Unhandled Exceptions
rules.when: Unhandled exceptions occur in the application
rules.then: Verify that a "last resort" error handler is defined which will catch all unhandled exceptions. This is both to avoid losing error details that must go to log files and to ensure that an error does not take down the entire application process, leading to a loss of availability.
exceptions: Certain languages, (including Swift, Go, and through common design practice, many functional languages,) do not support exceptions or last-resort event handlers.
